record.paper_title: Some Open Questions about Symplectic 4-Manifolds, Singular Plane Curves, and Braid Group Factorizations
record.original_question: Fix a symmetric-group-valued morphism θ and let LB_d(θ) be the subgroup of the braid group B_d consisting of braids b such that θ ∘ b_* = θ, where b_* is the induced automorphism of the punctured-fiber fundamental group. Determine whether an analogue of Kharlamov-Kulikov stabilization holds inside LB_d(θ): namely, whether any two factorizations in LB_d(θ) of the same braid element, with the same numbers of factors of each type, become equivalent after appending enough copies of a suitable standard factorization and then applying Hurwitz moves.

evidence.quote: Question 4.4. Given a symmetric group valued morphism θ, does a statement similar to Theorem 4.3 hold for factorizations in LB_d(θ)?
Then the liftable braid group is LB_d(θ) = {b ∈ B_d, θ ◦ b_* = θ}.

Theorem 4.3 (Kharlamov-Kulikov). Let F and F′ be two factorizations of the same element in B_d, with the same numbers of factors of each type. Then there exists an integer n such that the factorizations F · (F_0)^n and F′ · (F_0)^n are equivalent under Hurwitz moves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_d$ denote the Artin braid group on $d$ strands, acting on the free group $F_d = \pi_1(D^2 \setminus \{p_1,\dots,p_d\})$ via the standard (right) action $b \mapsto b_*$ on the punctured-disk fundamental group. Fix a surjective homomorphism $\theta : F_d \to S_n$ to the symmetric group on $n$ letters that sends each meridian generator $x_i$ to a transposition, and define the liftable braid group
$$LB_d(\theta) = \{\, b \in B_d : \theta \circ b_* = \theta \,\}.$$
A factorization in $LB_d(\theta)$ is an ordered tuple $F = (b_1,\dots,b_r)$ of elements $b_i \in LB_d(\theta)$, each lying in a prescribed conjugacy class (the "type" of $b_i$); its product is $b_1 \cdots b_r \in LB_d(\theta)$. Two factorizations of the same length are Hurwitz-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of Hurwitz moves
$$(\dots,b_i,b_{i+1},\dots) \leftrightarrow (\dots, b_i b_{i+1} b_i^{-1}, b_i, \dots), \qquad (\dots,b_i,b_{i+1},\dots) \leftrightarrow (\dots, b_{i+1}, b_{i+1}^{-1} b_i b_{i+1},\dots).$$
Concatenation of factorizations is denoted by $\cdot$. The Kharlamov–Kulikov stabilization theorem asserts: there exists a fixed standard factorization $F_0$ in $B_d$ such that for any two factorizations $F, F'$ in $B_d$ of the same element and with the same multiset of factor types, there exists an integer $n \ge 0$ for which $F \cdot F_0^n$ and $F' \cdot F_0^n$ are Hurwitz-equivalent.

Question: Does the analogous statement hold inside $LB_d(\theta)$? That is, does there exist a standard factorization $F_0$ (in $LB_d(\theta)$) such that, for any two factorizations $F, F'$ in $LB_d(\theta)$ of the same element of $LB_d(\theta)$ and with the same multiset of factor types, some integer $n \ge 0$ makes $F \cdot F_0^n$ and $F' \cdot F_0^n$ Hurwitz-equivalent within $LB_d(\theta)$?

The status appears unresolved in publicly indexed literature.
